body: import { type RouteConfig, route, index, layout } from '@react-router/dev/routes'
routes.ts config.description:
**Framework mode.** `app/routes.ts` — the route manifest for Framework mode.
The default export must satisfy `RouteConfig`.

routes: index().description: **Framework mode.** The route rendered at the parent's exact path. An index route has no path of its own.

routes: route().description:
**Framework mode.** A path segment mapped to a route module.
Pass a fourth argument (array) for nested children.

routes: route() with children.description: **Framework mode.** Nested routes. The parent renders an `<Outlet />` for its children.

routes: layout().description:
**Framework mode.** Wraps children in a layout component without adding a path segment.
Use it for shared chrome (sidebars, auth shells) that should not appear in the URL.

routes: prefix().description:
**Framework mode.** Prepends a path segment to a set of routes without introducing a layout component.
Spread it into the array — it returns a list, not a single route.

routes: dynamic segment.description:
**Framework mode.** `:param` captures a URL segment, readable as `params.${2:id}` in the loader and component.
Append `?` (`:id?`) to make it optional.

routes: splat route.description:
**Framework mode.** `*` matches the rest of the URL, available as `params['*']`.
A bare `route('*', ...)` at the top level is the usual 404 handler.
